judged_text: The added token refresh (fetch plus prisma.credential.update) runs unconditionally inside the connection-creation path with no expiry guard, where the previous code made no remote call or DB write when building the jsforce connection (jsforce refreshed lazily on 401). Every time a SalesforceCalendarService builds its connection (once per service instantiation, i.e. per calendar operation), the app now makes a Salesforce token-refresh HTTP call and a credential DB write even when the stored token is still valid — added latency and write amplification on a previously call-free path; an isExpired guard would preserve the refresh intent without the cost.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new code performs a refresh-token HTTP request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token" ...)`) and then writes updated credentials to the DB (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) unconditionally during service/connection setup, before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no expiry/validity guard shown in the diff, so each instantiation/path that builds the connection will incur network latency and a DB write even if the existing access token is still usable. This is a concrete performance/write-amplification concern introduced by the change, not necessarily a correctness bug.
